description: Every operation of the OpenCRS core and where each caller exposes it. Each binding's test suite checks its own exports against this file: every name listed must exist, every public call must be listed (here or under helpers), and a binding with no name for an operation must have an entry in exceptions saying why. To add an operation, add it here with a name for every binding; the suites fail until each binding has it. The README's table of calls is this file in prose.

bindings.go: exported functions of the package at the repo root
bindings.js: properties of the object js/opencrs.js's load() returns

version.summary: Tool, spec and rule pack versions

lint.summary: Check a document against the schemas

probe.summary: Read a file's type, pixels, size and duration
probe.note: Go reads an io.ReaderAt and the browser takes bytes; npm and Python take a path and, separately, bytes; the CLI takes paths.

check.summary: Check creative against the screens it targets
check.note: Where a binding has two names, the second probes the files named in the manifest under a directory; the browser has no directory and passes the files to check.

resolve.summary: Show a format's or a screen's requirements

resolve_strictest.summary: One set of requirements for every screen a reference covers

publisher.summary: Check a publisher's index and documents, from pages already fetched

fetch_publisher.summary: Fetch a publisher's documents (SSRF-safe), say which to trust, and run the publisher check
fetch_publisher.note: npm and Python also have discover, the trust decisions alone, as `opencrs fetch` prints them; Go's FetchPublisher carries them in its result's Discovery. The CLI's fetch is the trust decisions and its publisher is the whole check.

legibility.summary: Minimum text size for a viewing distance

dwell.summary: What a driver can read of a sign at a speed, and each rule pack's limits

rule_packs.summary: List the built-in rule packs and their limits

conformance.summary: Run the conformance suite against a validator

exceptions.cli.publisher: The command line has no pages to pass in; its `publisher` command fetches them itself (see fetch_publisher).
exceptions.js.fetch_publisher: A browser can't fetch other sites: CORS stops it reading a publisher's files. Fetch them yourself and pass them to publisher.
exceptions.go.conformance: The conformance suite runs only in the CLI. Go, JavaScript and the native bindings are tested against its cases by their own suites.
exceptions.js.conformance: The conformance suite runs only in the CLI.
exceptions.npm.conformance: The conformance suite runs only in the CLI.
exceptions.python.conformance: The conformance suite runs only in the CLI.
